title: Business-provider APIs rebuilt as governed agent tools
subtitle: Payments, email/CRM and social-publishing APIs, rebuilt operation by operation as governed agent tools under stable names, with credentials server-side, attribution where it round-trips and every call accounted.

stats.label: agent tools behind the FAFOHive gateway
provider keys in any agent's context

lede: Identity, attribution and durable accounting are designed in rather than bolted on. The services belong to the providers; the tools, the gateway, the capability tables and the attribution model are mine. FAFOHive gives managed agents a payments provider, an email/CRM provider and a social-publishing provider as tools, and I decided no agent would ever hold a provider key. The tools are mine: each provider's API was rebuilt, operation by operation, as a tool contract with a stable name, so the surface agents see is designed rather than inherited. My own X, Facebook and Reddit modules join through the same gateway under the same trust model, so agents see one surface. See Agents with real tools and no keys.
quote: Unclassified operations stay usable and accounted; blocking them would break agents on every provider change.
evidence: Tool synthesis and governed API integration: payments, email and CRM, and social publishing APIs rebuilt operation by operation as 354 agent tools under stable names.
Identity and least privilege for AI agents: the calling assignment derived from authentication on the server, never from tool input, and 0 provider keys in any agent's context.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: every provider call accounted through an outbox whose replay after a restart never calls the provider twice.
Data provenance and attribution: operation-level capability tables bound to each API version decide when attribution is stamped and whether an object was created or only referenced.
author: Corey James
